content.rationale: S5-bracket fixes the protocol — the op head read before the operation runs and again after, the run itself untouched — S5-lifecycle which invocations feed it, G-capture and G-footprint (xwnylypn) that the window's entries attributed to the invoking workspace are what a bracket keeps, and S5-observation (urqytyqn) that the bracket settles the working copy once before its window and that the reads leave it alone; M-layout places the module flat at src/markers_capture.rs. A recording additionally snapshots the target's owned paths before and after the run and stores one journal entry (S5-journal-capture, wxtzltkt) through M-journal (zutqsqtu), so the marker's recording entry names that entry. It crosses M-jj's runner and reads the head, the window and the invoking workspace through M-jj-oplog, appends through M-markers-append, and names the store and the carried reasons through M-store and M-markers-persist. One transition: settle the working copy once (`jj util snapshot`) before the pre-read, read the live op head, run the given operation untouched, read the head again, keep the window's entries that are the invoking workspace's own — so another workspace's entries that share the window are not the operation's, and a snapshot of edits that predate the invocation is outside the window rather than in it. A failed settle or read aborts before the run, so nothing is bracketed that never opened; the run's own outcome passes through unexamined, so which invocation brackets stays the caller's call and every failure is carried, never rendered. The run answers the target it named (S5-record-named, wotmvzyt); one that answers none closes its bracket and records nothing — no entries are kept and no marker is appended — and one whose window kept no entries records nothing too, so a no-op buys no un-undoable step and the marker file is left as it stood; a run that names a target and kept work records even when it fails, because that work landed before the refusal.
